I need to work out the transformation rule: the least common color (red, 2) marks cells that should stay unchanged, while the background fill turns other cells into 4, regardless of their original color. I'm checking the example grid to confirm that black cells also get converted when they're part of the backdrop rather than the red markers.

Now I'm designing test grids with a background of 5s and scattered 0s, making sure my red clusters' bounding boxes don't accidentally include stray 0s that would confuse the pattern. I'm working out the grouping rule: two red cells belong to the same cluster if both their row and column offsets are within 2, and clusters need to be spaced far enough apart (offsets greater than 2) to stay distinct. I'm placing cluster A at rows/cols 1-3 and cluster B around rows 6-8, checking each pairwise distance to confirm the clustering logic holds.

Finishing the grid rows and verifying both bounding boxes are clean of zeros, confirming clusters A and B check out. Now I'm planning a second grid with three clusters, considering swapping the background color for more variety.

Still filling in the grid values...

I'm now verifying the bounding boxes I found against the grid: box B at rows5-7/cols7-9, box C at rows9-10/cols2-4, and box A at rows1-2/cols1-3 all check out. Moving to a third grid, I'm spotting two clusters plus a vertical pair and starting to map their coordinates.

I'm filling out the rest of the grid rows and verifying the bounding boxes for clusters B and C match the pattern of 2s I expect, checking row by row that the values line up correctly.
